output:
@Kavya, I wish we had spoken before this became a LinkedIn conversation. But with people tagging me on your post, I want to own my mistake and clear up a few facts, without turning this into a fight.

We were both in Foundry91 cohort 4, with demo day in March 2026. You’re building SitterNest, a babysitter booking app. I’m building DabbaDost, for home tiffin subscriptions. We’ve shared more than a batch WhatsApp group.

Before demo day, you sat with me till 1am in our Koramangala office, fixing our Razorpay webhook mess. I haven’t forgotten that. A hiring disagreement doesn’t erase what your friendship and help have meant to me.

First, the part I got wrong: I knew from day one where both candidates worked. I should have called you before making the offers, not told you after the second offer was accepted. I sent a WhatsApp when I should have had a conversation much earlier. That’s on me, and I’m sorry.

I also need to correct three things, because leaving them unanswered lets a version that isn’t true keep spreading.

We posted an open backend developer role on our LinkedIn page and Instahyre on 14 September. The first candidate applied on 19 September. The second came through his referral two weeks later. Nobody from my side DMed either of them to recruit them.

The offers were 22% above their respective current CTCs, not 40%. Both joined us on 3 November.

We also have an ESOP pool. It is small, but it is real and has been on paper since January. The claim that we promised ESOPs we don’t have is not correct.

I’m not naming either person. They didn’t ask to be part of a public dispute, and I don’t want this discussion to become about them.

Those facts don’t cancel out my responsibility to have called you first. Equally, I hope we can separate that mistake from claims about how the hiring happened.

There are 11 startups in our batch, hiring from the same small pool in HSR and Koramangala. This will come up again. My suggestion for our cohort: if you’re interviewing someone from another batch company, give that founder a heads-up before making an offer. Not a request for permission, just a direct conversation so nobody hears it after the fact.

Kavya, I respect you and want to sort this out with you, not win a comment thread. Coffee or a call is open this week, whenever you’re okay with it.
